open_points.subject: owner form reader handling of unlisted submitted fields
open_points.question: When a submitted form contains a field for which the owner form table has no row, must the owner interface reject the request, ignore that field, or preserve it as an untyped value?
options: Reject the submission as invalid.
Ignore every unlisted field.
Accept and preserve unlisted fields.

witness.initial: The release table contains only a row named "name".
events: The owner submits fields named "name" and "unexpected".
The owner interface reads the submission.
outcomes: The interface refuses the submission because "unexpected" has no table row.
The interface ignores "unexpected" and continues using "name".
witness.observer: The owner sees either a refusal or a successful operation.

open_points.subject: uniqueness and ambiguity of owner form field names
open_points.question: Must field names be unique across the whole table, or may the same name occur once for the request and once for its values; if duplicates are forbidden, what must the Required tests item show about rejection of such a release?
options: Require globally unique names and refuse a release containing duplicates.
Require uniqueness only within each of request and values.
Allow duplicates and define deterministic row-selection precedence.
open_points.default_guess: Require globally unique names, refuse a release containing duplicates, and require a test showing that duplicate names cannot be released.

witness.initial: The table has two rows named "limit", one belonging to the request and one belonging to its values.
events: The page submits one field named "limit" with text "5".
The owner interface looks up the row and reads the field.
outcomes: The release is invalid because names must be globally unique.
The interface accepts the release and assigns the submitted value to one or both destinations.
witness.observer: The owner and the resulting operation see whether the form is available and where the value is assigned.

open_points.subject: destination represented by request-versus-values membership
open_points.text: whether it belongs to the owner's request itself or to the values the owner gives
open_points.question: For a named field, what exact result must reading it produce: a top-level entry keyed by the field name, a value at some separately defined path, or another structure; and what happens when the required destination cannot represent that field?
options: Use the field name as a top-level key in either the request or its values.
Resolve a path supplied by another declared source of truth.
Refuse fields whose destination cannot be determined.
open_points.default_guess: Use the field name as a top-level key in the selected destination and refuse a release whose destination cannot represent it.

witness.initial: The table contains a request field named "owner.name", but no path or nesting rule is stated.
events: The owner enters "Ada" in that field.
The interface constructs the owner request.
outcomes: The request contains the literal top-level key "owner.name" with value "Ada".
The request contains an object "owner" whose "name" member is "Ada".
witness.observer: The operation consuming the constructed request sees a different request shape.

open_points.subject: whole-number parsing
open_points.question: Which textual forms count as a whole number, what numeric range and representation result, and what refusal is required for an empty, malformed, signed, prefixed, or out-of-range value?
options: Accept canonical unsigned decimal digits only.
Accept signed decimal integer syntax.
Use the runtime's general integer parser, including any prefixes or whitespace it accepts.
open_points.default_guess: Accept optional surrounding whitespace followed by canonical signed base-10 digits, produce an arbitrary-precision integer, and refuse any other or out-of-range representation.

witness.initial: A table row says that field "count" is read as a whole number.
outcomes: The interface accepts the text and produces the integer 1.
The interface refuses the submission as a noncanonical whole number.
witness.observer: The owner sees success or refusal.

open_points.subject: yes-or-no parsing
open_points.question: Which submitted texts represent yes and no, whether matching is case-sensitive or localized, and what refusal is required for every other text?
options: Accept only the exact strings "yes" and "no".
Accept conventional boolean strings such as true/false and yes/no case-insensitively.
Accept only values explicitly stored in the release table.
open_points.default_guess: Accept only exact release-defined values; because none are currently defined, add exact canonical yes and no spellings and refuse all others.

witness.initial: A table row says that field "enabled" is read as yes or no.
outcomes: The interface refuses "true" because only "yes" denotes yes.
witness.observer: The owner sees success or refusal.

open_points.subject: closed-list selection and parsing
open_points.text: as one of a closed list
open_points.question: Where is the particular closed list for each field identified, are submitted member names or member values accepted, and what refusal is required for a value outside that list?
options: Add the applicable enumeration or closed-list identity to every such row and accept its member values.
Use one global closed list for all such rows.
Infer the list from the destination field's later contract.
open_points.default_guess: Add an explicit closed-list identity to each applicable row, accept only its declared member values, and refuse every other value.

witness.initial: The table contains a field "status" whose text is read as one of a closed list, while releases define both status and role lists.
outcomes: The interface refuses "admin" because it is not in the status list.
The interface accepts "admin" after selecting the role list.
witness.observer: The owner and the request consumer see refusal versus a populated value.

open_points.subject: representation and exported symbol of the owner form table
open_points.text: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
open_points.question: What generated provider symbol and row representation expose this table to modules that read it?
options: Keep the previously named imported constant `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` and generate rows carrying the stated facts.
Generate a different explicitly declared imported constant and update every consuming note to name it.
Keep the table as a design-only fact and generate no reader, if no generated module consumes it.
consequences: Keeping `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` preserves a stable import name while requiring generation to define the revised, reduced row shape.
Choosing another symbol requires all consumers to use that exact imported name and risks drift from earlier assumptions about `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS`.
Keeping it outside the specification is valid only if generated code does not read the table; otherwise the code has no path to the decided value.
open_points.requirement: The release: the owner form table the data provider holds.
open_points.default_guess: Generate the imported `OWNER_FORM_FIELDS` constant with rows containing exactly the revised facts.
